be a \(2\times 2\) matrix and \(T\) denote the corresponding transformation of the plane.

(a) How many invariant lines does \(T\) have? Denote the two scaling factors as \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) where \(\lambda_1 \le \lambda_2\).

(b) \(\lambda_1 = \) [student response field]

(c) The parametric vector form of the invariant line \(E_1\) associated to \(\lambda_1\) is \(E_1 = \{\, t\,\text{[vector]}\mid t \in \mathbb{R}\}\).

(d) \(\lambda_2 = \) [student response field]

Page 4

“Simple” Systems – Linear Algebra Version

Let the standard basis vectors be \(\vec{e}_1 = \begin{bmatrix}1\\0\end{bmatrix}\) and \(\vec{e}_2 = \begin{bmatrix}0\\1\end{bmatrix}\).

NameSystem (Matrix Form)General Solution
Uncoupled \(\vec{r}\,' = \begin{bmatrix}a&0\\0&b\end{bmatrix}\vec{r}\) \(\vec{r}(t) = C\,\vec{e}_1\,e^{at} + D\,\vec{e}_2\,e^{bt}\)
Partially Coupled \(\vec{r}\,' = \begin{bmatrix}a&1\\0&a\end{bmatrix}\vec{r}\) \(\vec{r}(t) = \bigl(C\,\vec{e}_1 + D(\vec{e}_1\,t + \vec{e}_2)\bigr)e^{at}\)
Complex Uncoupled \(\vec{r}\,' = \begin{bmatrix}a&-b\\b&a\end{bmatrix}\vec{r}\) \(\vec{r}(t) = C_1\bigl(\cos(bt)\,\vec{e}_1 + \sin(bt)\,\vec{e}_2\bigr)e^{at} + C_2\bigl(-\sin(bt)\,\vec{e}_1 + \cos(bt)\,\vec{e}_2\bigr)e^{at}\)

Page 5

Systems – Linear Algebra Version (General Basis)

Let \(\vec{v}\) and \(\vec{w}\) be basis vectors with change-of-basis matrix \(P = [\vec{v} \mid \vec{w}]\).

NameSystemGeneral Solution
Uncoupled \(\vec{r}\,' = P\begin{bmatrix}a&0\\0&b\end{bmatrix}P^{-1}\vec{r}\) \(\vec{r}(t) = C\,\vec{v}\,e^{at} + D\,\vec{w}\,e^{bt}\)
Partially Coupled \(\vec{r}\,' = P\begin{bmatrix}a&1\\0&a\end{bmatrix}P^{-1}\vec{r}\) \(\vec{r}(t) = \bigl(C\,\vec{v} + D(\vec{v}\,t + \vec{w})\bigr)e^{at}\)
Complex Uncoupled \(\vec{r}\,' = P\begin{bmatrix}a&-b\\b&a\end{bmatrix}P^{-1}\vec{r}\) \(\vec{r}(t) = C_1\bigl(\cos(bt)\,\vec{v} + \sin(bt)\,\vec{w}\bigr)e^{at} + C_2\bigl(-\sin(bt)\,\vec{v} + \cos(bt)\,\vec{w}\bigr)e^{at}\)

Note: \(\vec{e}_1\) is sent to \(\vec{v}\) and \(\vec{e}_2\) is sent to \(\vec{w}\).

Page 6

SMDs and First-Order Systems – Phase Planes

Which phase plane corresponds to the system of differential equations \(\vec{r}\,'(t) = A\vec{r}(t)\) where

\[ A = \begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0\\0 & -1\end{bmatrix}? \]

This is already in diagonal (uncoupled) form with \(a = -2\) and \(b = -1\). Both eigenvalues are negative, so the origin is a stable node (sink). Trajectories flow in along both axes, faster in the \(x\)-direction.

Four candidate vector field diagrams are shown in a 2×2 grid, each on axes ranging from approximately −4 to 4. The correct diagram shows arrows pointing inward toward the origin from all directions, with flow along the horizontal axis decaying faster than along the vertical axis, consistent with eigenvalues −2 and −1.

Page 7

SMDs and First-Order Systems – Phase Planes (continued)

Which phase plane corresponds to \(\vec{r}\,'(t) = A\vec{r}(t)\) where

\[ A = \begin{bmatrix}-2 & 1\\0 & -2\end{bmatrix}? \]

This is an upper-triangular matrix with repeated eigenvalue \(a = -2\) and an off-diagonal shear entry. It is in partially coupled (Jordan) form. The origin is a degenerate stable node: all trajectories approach the origin tangent to the \(x\)-axis (the \( ec{e}_1\)-direction).

Four candidate vector field diagrams are shown. The correct diagram displays arrows curving inward toward the origin, with trajectories becoming tangent to the horizontal axis as they approach the origin, characteristic of a repeated-eigenvalue sink with a shear term.

Page 8

SMDs and First-Order Systems – Phase Planes (continued)

Which phase plane corresponds to \(\vec{r}\,'(t) = A\vec{r}(t)\) where

\[ A = \begin{bmatrix}-2 & 1\\-1 & -2\end{bmatrix}? \]

This matrix is in complex uncoupled form with \(a = -2\) and \(b = 1\). The origin is a spiral sink: trajectories spiral inward toward the origin.

Four candidate vector field diagrams are shown. The correct diagram displays arrows spiraling inward toward the origin in a counterclockwise direction, consistent with a negative real part \(a = -2\) (decay) and imaginary part \(b = 1\) (rotation).

Page 9

SMDs and First-Order Systems – Phase Planes (continued)

Which phase plane corresponds to \(\vec{r}\,'(t) = A\vec{r}(t)\) where

\[ A = \begin{bmatrix}2&-2\\2&2\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}-1&0\\0&-2\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}2&-2\\2&2\end{bmatrix}^{-1}? \]

This SMD has \(a = -1\) and \(b = -2\) with a non-standard basis. Both eigenvalues are negative, so the origin is a stable node (sink), but the invariant lines are aligned with the columns of \(P\) rather than the standard axes.

Four candidate vector field diagrams are shown. The correct diagram shows arrows flowing inward toward the origin, with two invariant lines (the eigenvector directions from \(P\)) visible as straight trajectories. The flow along one invariant line is faster than the other, consistent with the two distinct negative eigenvalues.

Page 10

SMDs and First-Order Systems – Phase Planes (continued)

Which phase plane corresponds to \(\vec{r}\,'(t) = A\vec{r}(t)\) where

\[ A = \begin{bmatrix}1&-4\\2&1\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}-1&1\\0&-1\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}1&-4\\2&1\end{bmatrix}^{-1}? \]

This SMD has a repeated eigenvalue \(a = -1\) with the partially coupled (Jordan block) structure in the \(B\)-matrix. The origin is a degenerate stable node relative to the basis given by the columns of \(P = \begin{bmatrix}1&-4\\2&1\end{bmatrix}\).

Four candidate vector field diagrams are shown. The correct diagram shows arrows spiraling or curving toward the origin, all becoming tangent to the \( ec{v}_1 = \begin{bmatrix}1\\2\end{bmatrix}\) direction as \(t\to\infty\), in contrast to the standard-basis partially coupled case where they become tangent to the \(x\)-axis.

Page 11

SMDs and First-Order Systems – Phase Planes (continued)

Which phase plane corresponds to \(\vec{r}\,'(t) = A\vec{r}(t)\) where

\[ A = \begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\2&2\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}1&-2\\2&1\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\2&2\end{bmatrix}^{-1}? \]

This SMD has \(a = 1\) and \(b = 2\) in the complex uncoupled \(B\)-matrix, so trajectories form a spiral source: they spiral outward from the origin, growing in amplitude due to \(a = 1 > 0\).

Four candidate vector field diagrams are shown. The correct diagram displays arrows spiraling outward from the origin, consistent with a positive real part \(a = 1\) (growth) and imaginary part \(b = 2\) (rotation). The spiraling occurs relative to the coordinate grid defined by the columns of \(P\).

Page 12

Examples – Reading Off the General Solution

Consider the system \(\vec{r}\,'(t) = A\vec{r}(t)\) where

\[ A = \begin{bmatrix}-7 & 0\\0 & -2\end{bmatrix}. \]

Fill in the missing vectors in the general solution below, where \(C\) and \(D\) are constants.

Since \(A\) is diagonal with \(a = -7\) and \(b = -2\), the system is already in uncoupled form with standard basis vectors \(\vec{e}_1 = \begin{bmatrix}1\\0\end{bmatrix}\) and \(\vec{e}_2 = \begin{bmatrix}0\\1\end{bmatrix}\). The general solution is:

\[ \vec{r}(t) = C\begin{bmatrix}1\\0\end{bmatrix}e^{-7t} + D\begin{bmatrix}0\\1\end{bmatrix}e^{-2t}. \]

Examples – General Solution with SMD

Consider the system \(\vec{r}\,'(t) = A\vec{r}(t)\) where

\[ A = \begin{bmatrix}3 & 4\\\tfrac{1}{2} & 2\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}4 & -4\\1 & 2\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}4 & 0\\0 & 1\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}4 & -4\\1 & 2\end{bmatrix}^{-1}. \]

Find the general solution \(\vec{r}(t) = \begin{bmatrix}x(t)\\y(t)\end{bmatrix}\). Use \(C\) and \(D\) for the constants.

The SMD is of uncoupled type with \(a = 4\), \(b = 1\), \(\vec{v} = \begin{bmatrix}4\\1\end{bmatrix}\), and \(\vec{w} = \begin{bmatrix}-4\\2\end{bmatrix}\). The general solution is:

\[ \vec{r}(t) = C\begin{bmatrix}4\\1\end{bmatrix}e^{4t} + D\begin{bmatrix}-4\\2\end{bmatrix}e^{t}. \]

Reading off the components:

\[ x(t) = 4Ce^{4t} - 4De^{t}, \\ y(t) = Ce^{4t} + 2De^{t}. \]
